name: Opus Value
strategy: Quality-momentum / trend-following: own demonstrated relative-strength leaders (momentum & quality factor ETFs + top above-200dma names) with income/quality ballast and hard stops.

positions.thesis: Raised 12 -> 16 and now the largest position, because Jackson Hole confirmed the regime argument I already had rather than changing it. Warsh pledging to return inflation to 2% and signalling higher rates means the cost of capital is going up, not down, and this fund holds precisely the businesses least exposed to that: high return on equity funded internally, so they never need the market that just got more expensive. The price supports it too, quietly — 223.62, up 0.2% on the week and 1.6% below its 52-week high, while the dedicated momentum factor fell 1.8% and is down 5.5% over two weeks. Holding flat while momentum breaks is relative strength by omission, and it is the second week running that this divergence has appeared, which is what turns an observation into a signal. I raise it rather than parking the money in cash because a trend book that responds to a policy shock by hoarding cash is just market-timing with extra steps. Stop stays at -10%.

New 14%, and it is the largest single change I am making because it is the clearest leadership event of the week by an enormous margin. IGV gained 7.7% in the 08-27 session alone (102.39 to 110.32) and 5.9% on the week, is up 17.4% over four weeks, and closed 109.50 — 16.9% above its 200dma and 7.0% below its 52-week high. What makes it a trend rather than a one-day gap is breadth and cause: the move was led by names that did not report (OKTA +23% on the week, VEEV +11.6%, TEAM +10.8%, WDAY +29.5% over four weeks, SAP +22.5%), which means a narrative re-rating of the whole group, not an earnings pop. The cause is checkable — Salesforce's record quarter with cRPO +14%, best net-new order value in four years and Agentforce ARR at $1.5bn, publicly refuting the AI-destroys-SaaS thesis that de-rated the sector all year — and it directly displaces the group that stopped leading, with SMH down 7.7% over thirteen weeks against IGV up 7.7%. I take it as an ETF rather than single names precisely because I am buying a narrative reversal across a cohort, not any one company's quarter. The stop is -10% (about 98.5), set deliberately below the 102.39 gap origin so a complete gap fill does not eject me, but a failure of the whole move does.

Trimmed 13 -> 12, a one-point reduction that is bookkeeping rather than a change of view. At 34.90 it slipped 0.6% while SPY rose 0.5%, its first week of underperformance since I reclassified it from ballast to a trend I already own, and it remains 0.9% below its high with a 27.7% twelve-month return and a 12.8% cushion over its 200dma. That is still relative strength; it is simply no longer the standout it was, so it funds a point of the software initiation. The structural job is unchanged and still needed: a 0.69 beta and a 3.04% yield against a book that still carries 27% in miners, energy and bitcoin, and its Abbott, Amgen and Merck weights keep me in the pharma complex. Stop unchanged at -10%.

Cut 16 -> 11. I raised this to 16% on a breakout and the breakout ran into a policy wall five sessions later: Warsh's hawkish speech pushed September hike odds from ~34% to ~60%, the dollar rose 1.0%, and GDX fell 3.9% in that single session to close 99.65, back inside the 88-102 range it had cleared and down 3.1% on the week. I do not exit, and the reason is that this is still one of the strongest verified trends I own — up 34.5% over four weeks, 71.0% over twelve months, 11.6% above its 200dma and 14.0% below its 117.18 high, so there is still ground to reclaim. But 16% was sized on the assumption that the debasement driver was intact, and it took a direct hit from the only person who can reprice it. Trimming five points is the difference between following a trend and refusing to notice that its cause changed. The stop stays at -13% (about 90) because it is correctly placed just under the range it is now retesting.

Cut 15 -> 10 on my own stated rule. I wrote that the commodity leads the equity and that I would follow the driver in both directions; the driver turned decisively, with WTI down 4.2% on the week to 83.40 and now 26.2% below its 52-week high, and the same rule that took this from 8% to 15% on rising crude has to take it back down on falling crude or it was never a rule. The equity has not confirmed the fall — XLE at 62.68 is off just 1.5% and still 1.7% below its high with a 46.5% twelve-month return — and that divergence is exactly the condition under which I want less, not more: when the equity holds while its input collapses, I am being paid to reduce rather than punished for it. I keep 10% because this remains the only sleeve that pays if the inflation re-acceleration Warsh just described as unimproved actually persists, which is now the Fed's own stated concern. Stop unchanged at -12%.

Held at 7% with the stop unchanged. It gave back 2.8% to 148.35 from 152.55 in a week when the whole healthcare sector cooled (XLV -2.0%), which is participation in a sector pullback rather than a break in the name: it is still 5.2% below its 52-week high, up 13.9% over four weeks, 23.4% over thirteen, 76.2% over twelve months and 26.8% above its 200dma. Nothing in those numbers says the trend ended. It also does the job I bought it for more than ever after this rebalance — with hard assets cut to 27% and software added at 20%, I need a large-cap defensive leader whose driver is drug approvals and pipeline rather than the real rate, and this is the only one on my screen making that claim on price. I do not add, because the four-week move is still something I am following rather than something I can explain, and that argues for an initiation weight with a hard stop, which is what -12% is.

New 6%, the single-name expression of the software breakout and the strongest verified relative strength in my whole screen. At 218.40 it gained 13.8% on the week, is up 106.7% over twelve months, sits 4.2% below its 52-week high and 55.5% above its 200dma. Unlike a sympathy move, this one is its own: the 08-26 print was the best quarter in the company's history — revenue $1.47bn up 26%, adjusted EPS $0.31 against $0.29, net-new ARR up 51%, and full-year guidance lifted to $5.99-6.01bn — with management attributing demand to AI-driven threats, which is the mirror image of the AI-destroys-software fear. That distinction matters for a trend book: I am buying a company whose numbers say AI expands its market, held alongside an ETF that expresses the same shift diluted. Sized at 6% rather than larger because it is a single name 55% above its own 200dma, which is where trends are real and also where they snap; the -15% stop is wider than my usual because that extension is precisely why an 8% leash would be noise.

Held at 6% with the -18% stop unchanged. At 43.90 it gained 0.5% while bitcoin eased 0.6% to 77,830 — consolidation after a 19.9% breakout week, which is what a healthy trend does, not what a failing one does. The test I set at entry still passes: 38.4% below its 71.82 52-week high, so this remains a trend resuming inside an old range rather than a vertical move into new air. I neither add nor cut. I do not add because the macro turned against the debasement channel this week and I have just cut gold miners for that exact reason, so increasing crypto with the same hand would be incoherent. I do not cut because 6% behind an 18% stop is already sized so that being wrong costs about a point of NAV, and the spot ETF rather than a perp remains deliberate: leverage that liquidates on a 5% adverse margin move turns a trend position into a timing bet.

Trimmed 8 -> 6, continuing the reduction I began last week for the same reason of consistency. Its NVIDIA, Apple, Microsoft and Micron weights make it megacap and semiconductor-complex exposure with capped upside, and that complex is still the group that stopped leading — SMH down 7.7% over thirteen weeks and 17.3% below its high, MTUM down 5.5% over two weeks. Having just exited SPMO and GOOGL on that reasoning, leaving this at 8% would quietly reinstate the exposure I keep deciding against. It held up fine on the week at 60.15, up 0.5%, which is why it is a trim and not an exit: the 10.78% distribution yield is genuinely counter-cyclical income that improves as dispersion between my directional sleeves rises, and I have just raised dispersion again by swapping ten points of hard assets for twenty points of software. Stop unchanged at -10%.

reassessment_note: Weekly desk 2026-08-29: Leadership rotated again and it was measurable in a single session. Enterprise software is now the strongest verified trend in the market: IGV rose 7.7% on 08-27 alone and 5.9% on the week, is up 17.4% over four weeks, sits 16.9% above its 200dma and only 7.0% below its 52-week high — driven by a checkable fundamental event, Salesforce's record quarter and guidance raise, plus CrowdStrike's best quarter ever with net-new ARR up 51%. Simultaneously the hard-asset sleeve I built to 37% took a direct policy hit: Warsh pushed September hike odds to roughly 60%, GDX fell 3.9% in a session, GLD 3.2%, and crude 4.2% to 26% below its 52-week high while XLE held — the driver diverging from the equity, and I said in writing I would follow the driver in both directions. So I cut hard assets from 37% to 27% and put 20% into the group that is demonstrably leading. Two exits are overdue on my own stated conditions rather than on new information. SPMO underperformed SPY again (-1.3% against +0.5%) after breaking the 151-155 consolidation I named as its hold condition, so the stub does not survive a second failed week. GOOGL was flat for a third straight week, is down 10.9% over thirteen and 13.9% below its high, and in a trend book flat is not a trend — I have now cut it twice rather than deciding, and deciding is cheaper than a fourth trim. I raise QUAL to 16% because Warsh handed me the strongest possible confirmation of the regime argument I already had: if the cost of capital is going up rather than down, high-return-on-equity businesses with little leverage are the ones that never need to visit that market.
novelty: This book shares no symbol with my Round 2 book and expresses the opposite side of the same week's evidence: Round 2 harvested CRM into strength and holds the software complex only through its most damaged names (ORCL at 54% below its high, HUBS at 50% below), while this book buys the breakout itself through IGV and CRWD at 7% and 4% below their highs, pairs it with QUAL, SCHD and JEPQ ballast rather than cash, and expresses precious metals through the miners on a stop instead of bullion.
research_notes:
PRICE WORK (own pulls, 2y daily, all marks 2026-08-28 close; crypto truncated to 08-28 so I am not trading on weekend prints).

THE WEEK'S TWO EVENTS.

(1) The SaaS de-rating broke. Salesforce reported 2026-08-26 after the close: FY27 Q2 revenue $11.345bn (+10.8% y/y), adjusted EPS $5.90 versus roughly $3.27 expected, net income +73.3%, cRPO +14% cc to $33.5bn, best net-new annual order value in four years, attrition near a record low, FY guidance lifted to ~$46.25bn, Agentforce ARR $1.5bn. Benioff explicitly attacked the "SaaSpocalypse" narrative. The read-across was violent and broad: IGV +7.7% on 08-27 alone (102.39 -> 110.32) and +5.9% on the week, +17.4% over four weeks, now 16.9% above its 200dma and only 7.0% below its 52-week high. CRM 205.62 -> 252.05 -> 256.00 (+22.4% w/w). NOW 125.80 -> 144.71 (+12.6% w/w, helped by its own Tech Mahindra agentic-AI expansion). OKTA +23.0% w/w, CRWD +13.8%, VEEV +11.6%, TEAM +10.8%, HUBS +8.6%, ADBE +5.9%, SAP +1.3%/+22.5% 4w, WDAY +29.5% 4w. CrowdStrike's own print (08-26) was record: revenue $1.47bn +26%, net-new ARR +51%, FY guide raised to $5.99-6.01bn. This matters to me specifically because the AI-kills-software narrative is what made my Round 2 book cheap.

(2) Warsh's first Jackson Hole speech as Chair (08-28) was hawkish: "this summer's PCE and CPI readings... do not tell me that underlying trends have meaningfully improved," pledged return to 2%, signalled rates could go higher. September hike odds moved to ~57-60% from ~34%. Consequence in my book: GLD -3.2% in that single session (422.60 -> 408.89, -3.4% w/w), SLV -4.3%, GDX -3.9% on the day and -3.1% w/w, WTI -4.2% to 83.40 (26.2% below its 52-week high), UUP +1.0%, 10y 4.72%. The August debasement trade (gold's best month this century, ~+14%) took a direct policy hit.

NON-OBVIOUS TELL: TLT ROSE 1.0% on the week (82.05 -> 83.47 -> 82.88) into that hawkish shock. A credible inflation-fighter caps long-run inflation expectations, and hiking into 3.7% PCE raises the odds of the one outcome my books have no defence against. That is confirmation of the contrarian long-bond leg, not a contradiction.

POSITION-LEVEL VERIFICATION.
- ORCL 150.85 (+3.0% w/w), still 54.1% below its 52-week high. I flagged last week I could not verify the financing risk. Now I can, and it is WORSE, not better: BBB- downgrade, FY26 capex $55.7bn (from $21.2bn) funded with $43bn of debt plus $5bn equity, ~$40bn more to raise this year, and a six-month delay to the $165bn Project Jupiter pipeline reported 08-18. Offset: $75bn of prepaid/customer-supplied hardware reduces the raise. Base held (146.47 -> 150.85, higher low).
- UNH 392.95, +0.7% — the first higher weekly close in seven weeks. Group stabilised (HUM +1.8%, CI +0.5%, ELV -1.5%). Stop (~351 off the 398.76 entry) nowhere near.
- XLV 171.16 -2.0%, MRK 148.35 -2.8% — pharma cooled off the highs.
- SPMO 146.78 -1.3% against SPY +0.5%; MTUM -1.8% w/w, -5.5% 2w. The momentum factor still is not working; my stated "only if the break was noise" condition failed a second week.
- GOOGL 346.59 +0.5%, -10.9% over 13 weeks, 13.9% off its high — third straight flat week while everything I add to moves double digits.
- IBIT 43.90 +0.5%, BTC 77,830 -0.6% — orderly consolidation after the breakout, not a failure.

SCREENED AND REJECTED: SLV (43.2% below a 2026-01-28 blowoff high, but 13w -12.2% and falling into the same hawkish shock — a broken parabola, not a base). INTU (-49% off high, but FY27 guided to only 9-10% growth, below consensus, plus a securities-fraud investigation — fails the quality half of my mandate). NKE (39.60, still -14.3% over 13 weeks, 3% above its 52-week low, 23.9% below its 200dma — still making lower lows, still a pass). XBI (5-year highs and +80% 52w, but the cited driver is anticipated rate CUTS; Warsh just removed that, and it fell 2.0% this week). ADBE (re-entering above my own exit price on an unchanged thesis is churn). BABA, ALB, QCOM (all still declining).
